name: Tempester n°63: the five Release parameters never reach the voices above 123 (a release of 124-127 never ends in the Voice OS)
explanation: Why: the Voice OS envelope release steps by R = T[r] >> 7 with no minimum and T[124..127] < 0x80, so a Release of 124-127 never ends; only the next gate on that voice ends it. The Main's parameter table caps Amp Release (75) at 123 but lets Pitch (65), Filter (70), Aux 1 (83) and Aux 2 (91) Release reach 127. No Voice change: the Main caps what it sends. Every value reaches a voice through one of two senders, and both cap the five Releases at 123 while the stored value stays as it is: (1) [routine], the single-parameter word param << 8 | value (knobs, sliders, NRPN, CC, remote controls, all through knob_edit / [routine], [routine], [routine]; main loop), hook [address] to CAP_WORD; (2) the 0xF000 patch burst of [routine] (63 SRAM words of the sound, Timer 2), hook [address] to CAP_BURST, which redoes the Volume test of word 23 first and caps the Release byte of words 32 (Pitch, high), 35 (Filter, low), 37 (Amp, high), 41 (Aux 1, high) and 45 (Aux 2, high); it runs while the word just written shifts out. Sounds received, loaded or copied reach SRAM and are capped by these. The table maxima of 65, 70, 83 and 91 go from 127 to 123 ([address], [address], [address], [address]): the knob, NRPN and the display stop at 123. The load validator [routine] would reset a value above its new max to the default (0: an instant release, and the display draws nothing for a value above the max), so CAP_LOAD (hook [address]) makes an out-of-range Release its max (123) instead; every other parameter keeps the default rule. A stored sound with 124-127 therefore loads, shows and plays as 123, and its file keeps 124-127 until it is saved again. Not fixed (Voice side, Docs/plans/voice.md): a negative release modulation can push the index past 123 inside the voice. No RAM; 60 words at 0x9d07a300-0x9d07a3ef, 5 hook words, 4 table words. Proof: tools/sim_release_cap.py and its counter-proofs.

edits.why: j 0x9d07a3b0 ; validator, value above the max: was "lw s1,0x8(a3)" (moved to the delay slot)
delay slot: the default (was "sb s1,0x0(a2)", done by CAP_LOAD)
j 0x9d07a344 ; Timer 2 patch burst: was "beq a2,v1,[address]" (done by CAP_BURST). Delay slot "andi a1,t9,0xffff" kept
j 0x9d07a300 ; [routine]: was "or s0,s0,v0" (moved to the delay slot)
delay slot: word = param << 8 | value (was "andi a0,s0,0xffff", done by CAP_WORD)
andi t1,s0,0xff ; value. s0 = param << 8 | value; t0-t3 dead here (the routine then tail-calls [routine])
addiu t2,t0,-0x41 ; offset from Pitch Release (65)
delay slot: the instruction moved from [address]
bne a2,v1,0x9d07a354 ; v1 = 0x16: word 23 (Volume) goes to its handler, as before
addiu v0,a2,-0x1f ; delay slot: iteration - 31 (a1 = word 32, Pitch Release high byte)
li v1,0x2229 ; delay slot: bits 0, 3, 5, 9, 13 = iterations 31, 34, 36, 40, 44
beq v1,zero,0x9d07a3a8 ; no Release in this word
beq v0,v1,0x9d07a390 ; iteration 34: Filter Release, low byte
srl v0,a1,0x8 ; delay slot: high byte
ori a1,a1,0x7b00 ; delay slot: high byte 123
j [address] ; next iteration, where the Volume handler also returns
lui v0,0x9d07 ; a3 = table entry, a2 = the byte, s1 = default. v0 and t8 are dead in the validator loop
addiu v0,v0,0x3c00 ; entry of Pitch Release (65)
bne t8,zero,0x9d07a3e8 ; not 91 either: the default, as before
lw s1,0x4(a3) ; a Release: its max (123)
j [address] ; back in the validator loop
